thm:profile-union-honesty.proof_tex:
\textit{Proof.}
Every positive-rank member of \(\mathcal U\) satisfies \(\lVert M\rVert_\infty\leq B_{\max}\), and the only rank-zero matrix is zero.  Consequently every observed coordinate and every target value in the generating set for \(\overline{\mathcal K}\) lies in \([-B_{\max},B_{\max}]\).  Its closure is therefore compact and satisfies
\[
 \overline{\mathcal K}\subset[-B_{\max},B_{\max}]^{12}\times[-B_{\max},B_{\max}].
\tag{1}
\]
It follows that, whenever \(T(y)\neq\varnothing\), the infimum and supremum defining \(C_{\mathrm{prof}}(y)\) are finite and attained.  Equation (1) also gives
\(\operatorname{len}C_{\mathrm{prof}}(y)\leq2B_{\max}\).

We next verify measurability without imposing any unproved regularity on the union.  Let \(K_\mu\) be the projection of \(\overline{\mathcal K}\) onto its first twelve coordinates.  It is compact, and
\[
 \{y:T(y)\neq\varnothing\}=\{y:\operatorname{dist}(y,K_\mu)\leq\rho_\alpha\}
\tag{2}
\]
is closed.  For each real \(c\), the projections onto \(\mu\)-space of
\[
 \overline{\mathcal K}\cap\{(\mu,t):t\geq c\},
 \qquad
 \overline{\mathcal K}\cap\{(\mu,t):t\leq c\}
\]
are compact.  The events \(\{\sup T(y)\geq c\}\) and \(\{\inf T(y)\leq c\}\) are their respective closed \(\rho_\alpha\)-neighborhoods.  Together with (2) and the fixed value zero off (2), this proves that both endpoints are Borel measurable.  Thus \(C_{\mathrm{prof}}\) is a measurable nonempty connected closed interval rule.

Fix any \(M\in\mathcal U\), and put \(\mu=P_\Omega M\) and \(t=\tau(M)\).  The pair \((\mu,t)\) belongs to the generating set and hence to \(\overline{\mathcal K}\).  By the Gaussian sequence assumption,
\[
 \frac{n}{\sigma^2}\lVert Y-\mu\rVert_2^2\sim\chi^2_{12}.
\tag{3}
\]
The definition of \(q_{12,1-\alpha}\) and continuity of the chi-square distribution give
\[
 P_M\{\lVert Y-\mu\rVert_2\leq\rho_\alpha\}=1-\alpha.
\tag{4}
\]
On the event in (4), \(t\in T(Y)\), so \(t\in C_{\mathrm{prof}}(Y)\).  Therefore
\[
 \inf_{M\in\mathcal U}P_M\{\tau(M)\in C_{\mathrm{prof}}(Y)\}\geq1-\alpha,
\]
which proves \(C_{\mathrm{prof}}\in\mathfrak C_\alpha(\mathcal U)\).  Notice that no rank, strength, or orbit amplitude is supplied to the rule.

The pointwise length bound gives
\[
 E_{P_0}\operatorname{len}C_{\mathrm{prof}}(Y)\leq2B_{\max}.
\tag{5}
\]
Because \(C_{\mathrm{prof}}\) is union-honest, the definition of the rank-zero frontier gives the left inequality in the claimed ratio.  Theorem~\ref{thm:union-zero-lower} gives
\(\mathfrak L_0^{\mathcal U}(n)\geq B_{\max}(1-2\alpha)>0\); combining this with (5) proves the upper inequality.

Finally, the membership relation used by the endpoint programs is explicitly
\[
 (\mu,t)\in\overline{\mathcal K}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \forall\varepsilon>0\ \exists M\in\mathcal U:\
 \lVert P_\Omega M-\mu\rVert_2^2+|\tau(M)-t|^2<\varepsilon^2.
\tag{6}
\]
For the fixed four-by-four mask, membership in \(\mathcal U\) is a finite Boolean combination of entry bounds, vanishing and nonvanishing minors for ranks zero, one, or two, and the condition that the smallest positive singular value of the two-by-two anchor does not exceed \(B_{\max}\).  The last condition can itself be written with an auxiliary two-dimensional unit vector and polynomial inequalities.  Hence (6), together with
\(\lVert y-\mu\rVert_2^2\leq\rho_\alpha^2\), is a first-order formula over the reals in a fixed finite number of variables.  Quantifier elimination decides each endpoint sublevel query; bisection on the compact interval \([-B_{\max},B_{\max}]\) evaluates the two extrema to any prescribed accuracy. \(\square\)

defs.def:simultaneous-inversion-handle:
For a finite grid, let
\[
 \Theta_N=\{(\mu_i,t_i,k(i)):1\leq i\leq N\}
\]
mean that there is an \(M_i\in\mathcal U\) with \(\mu_i=P_\Omega M_i\) and \(t_i=\tau(M_i)\), and that \(k(i)=0\) for \(M_i\in\mathcal M_0\), while \(k(i)=(r,s)\) for \(M_i\in\mathcal M_r(s)\).  Put \(\mathcal T_N=\{t_i:1\leq i\leq N\}\) and
\[
 \mathcal A_N=\{[a,b]:a,b\in\mathcal T_N,\ a\leq b\}.
\]
The density of \(N(\mu_i,\sigma^2n^{-1}I_{12})\) is
\[
 f_i(y)=\left(\frac{n}{2\pi\sigma^2}\right)^6
 \exp\!\left\{-\frac{n}{2\sigma^2}\lVert y-\mu_i\rVert_2^2\right\}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal P_N\) be the set of Borel kernels \(p=(p_A:A\in\mathcal A_N)\) satisfying \(p_A(y)\geq0\) and \(\sum_Ap_A(y)=1\).  Define
\[
 Q_i(p)=\int_{\mathbb R^{12}}\sum_{A\in\mathcal A_N}
 \mathbf 1\{t_i\in A\}p_A(y)f_i(y)\,dy,
 \qquad
 R_i(p)=\int_{\mathbb R^{12}}\sum_{A\in\mathcal A_N}
 \operatorname{len}(A)p_A(y)f_i(y)\,dy,
\]
and, for each represented stratum label \(k\),
\[
 L_{k,N}=\inf_{p\in\mathcal P_N:\,Q_j(p)\geq1-\alpha\ \forall j}
 \max_{i:k(i)=k}R_i(p).
\]
Call the grid normalization-legal when \(L_{k,N}>0\) for every represented \(k\).  On such a grid the simultaneous finite-grid oracle factor is
\[
 \kappa_N^*=\inf_{\substack{\kappa\geq0,\ p\in\mathcal P_N}}
 \left\{\kappa:Q_i(p)\geq1-\alpha,\quad
 R_i(p)\leq\kappa L_{k(i),N}\quad(1\leq i\leq N)\right\}.
\]
For the continuum construction put
\[
 \overline{\mathcal K}=\operatorname{cl}\{(P_\Omega M,\tau(M)):M\in\mathcal U\}
 \subset\mathbb R^{12}\times\mathbb R,
 \qquad
 \rho_\alpha=\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt n}\sqrt{q_{12,1-\alpha}},
\]
where \(q_{12,1-\alpha}\) is the \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of a chi-square random variable with twelve degrees of freedom.  Define
\[
 T(y)=\{t:\text{there is }(\mu,t)\in\overline{\mathcal K}
 \text{ with }\lVert y-\mu\rVert_2\leq\rho_\alpha\},
 \qquad
 C_{\mathrm{prof}}(y)=
 \begin{cases}
 [\inf T(y),\sup T(y)],&T(y)\neq\varnothing,\\
 \{0\},&T(y)=\varnothing.
 \end{cases}
\]
The simultaneous-inversion handle consists of the finite-grid program \(\kappa_N^*\), its likelihood dual, and the continuum profile interval \(C_{\mathrm{prof}}\).

defs.def:rank-two-orbit: \[M_g(h,q)=\begin{pmatrix}hS&qR\\q\mathbf J R^{\mathsf T}S&(q^2/h)\mathbf J\end{pmatrix},\qquad g=(S,R)\in\mathcal H_2\times\mathcal H_2.\]
defs.def:admissible-orbit-amplitudes: \(\mathcal A_B=\{(h,q)\in(0,\infty)^2:h\le B_{\max},\ q\le B_{\max},\ q^2/h\le B_{\max}\}\).
defs.def:union-minimax-length: \(\mathfrak L_{0}^{\mathcal U}(n)=\inf_{C\in\mathfrak C_{\alpha}(\mathcal U)}E_{P_0}[\operatorname{len}C(Y)]\) and, for \(r\in\{1,2\}\) and \(s\in(0,B_{\max}]\), \(\mathfrak L_{r,s}^{\mathcal U}(n)=\inf_{C\in\mathfrak C_{\alpha}(\mathcal U)}\sup_{M\in\mathcal M_r(s)}E_{P_M}[\operatorname{len}C(Y)]\).

lem:block-completion-identification.proof_tex:
\textit{Proof.}
Fix \(M\in\mathcal M_r(s)\).  By the exact-rank assumptions,
\(\operatorname{rank}(M)=\operatorname{rank}(A)=r\).  Since \(A\) is a
submatrix of both \([A\ F]\) and \([A^{\mathsf T}\ G^{\mathsf T}]^{\mathsf T}\),
\[
r\leq \operatorname{rank}[A\ F]\leq \operatorname{rank}(M)=r,
\qquad
r\leq \operatorname{rank}\!\begin{bmatrix}A\\G\end{bmatrix}
\leq \operatorname{rank}(M)=r.
\]
Consequently \(\operatorname{col}(F)\subseteq\operatorname{col}(A)\) and
\(\operatorname{row}(G)\subseteq\operatorname{row}(A)\).  Thus there are
matrices \(X,Y_0\in\mathbb R^{2\times2}\) with \(F=AX\) and \(G=Y_0A\).
The Moore--Penrose identities give the particular choices
\(X=A^+F\) and \(Y_0=GA^+\).  Invertible block row and column operations now give
\[
\begin{pmatrix}I&0\\-Y_0&I\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}A&F\\G&D\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}I&-X\\0&I\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}A&0\\0&D-Y_0AX\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The left side has rank \(r\), whereas the right side has rank
\(r+\operatorname{rank}(D-Y_0AX)\).  Hence \(D=Y_0AX=GA^+F\).
Substitution into the definition of the causal target yields
\[
\tau(M)=\frac14\mathbf 1_2^{\mathsf T}GA^+F\mathbf 1_2.
\]
All matrices on the right are contained in the observed vector
\(P_{\Omega}M=\operatorname{vec}(A,F,G)\); the positive-strength condition
\(s>0\) fixes the rank and ensures that the Moore--Penrose inverse is evaluated
on the asserted exact-rank stratum.  This proves the stated identifying
functional. \(\square\)

snapshot.stmt: For every \(M\in\mathcal M_r(s)\), the missing block satisfies \(D=GA^{+}F\), where \(A^{+}\) is the Moore--Penrose inverse. Hence \(\tau(M)=\tfrac14\mathbf 1_2^{\mathsf T}GA^{+}F\mathbf 1_2\) is identified from \(P_{\Omega}M\) on each positive-strength stratum.

lem:orbit-membership.proof_tex:
\textit{Proof.}
Fix \((h,q)\in\mathcal A_B\) and \(g=(S,R)\in\mathcal G\).  Signed-permutation
matrices are orthogonal, so \(S^{-1}=S^{\mathsf T}\), and the anchor
\(A=hS\) has rank two with both singular values equal to \(h\).  Direct
multiplication gives
\[
GA^{-1}F
=q\mathbf J R^{\mathsf T}S\,(hS)^{-1}qR
=\frac{q^2}{h}\mathbf J R^{\mathsf T}SS^{\mathsf T}R
=\frac{q^2}{h}\mathbf J=D.
\]
Applying the same invertible block elimination used in the block-completion
lemma shows
\[
\operatorname{rank}M_g(h,q)
=\operatorname{rank}(hS)+
 \operatorname{rank}\{D-GA^{-1}F\}=2.
\]
Every nonzero entry of \(A\) has absolute value \(h\), every nonzero entry of
\(F\) has absolute value \(q\), every entry of
\(G=q\mathbf J R^{\mathsf T}S\) has absolute value \(q\), and every entry of
\(D\) equals \(q^2/h\).  The three inequalities in the definition of
\(\mathcal A_B\) therefore imply \(\lVert M_g(h,q)\rVert_\infty\leq B_{\max}\).
This proves \(M_g(h,q)\in\mathcal M_2(h)\).  Moreover,
\[
\tau(M_g(h,q))
=\frac14\mathbf 1_2^{\mathsf T}\frac{q^2}{h}\mathbf J\mathbf 1_2
=\frac{q^2}{h}.
\]
Finally, under the uniform law on
\(\mathcal H_2\times\mathcal H_2\), the matrices \(S\) and \(R\) are
independent and each has mean zero.  Hence
\[
E[S]=0,\qquad E[R]=0,\qquad
E[\mathbf J R^{\mathsf T}S]=\mathbf J E[R]^{\mathsf T}E[S]=0.
\]
The observation map retains precisely these three blocks, so averaging their
vectorizations proves \(64^{-1}\sum_g\mu_g(h,q)=0\). \(\square\)

snapshot.stmt: For every \((h,q)\in\mathcal A_B\) and \(g=(S,R)\in\mathcal G\), the construction \(M_g(h,q)\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_2(h)\), obeys \(D=GA^{-1}F=(q^2/h)\mathbf J\), and has \(\tau(M_g(h,q))=q^2/h\). Moreover, \(64^{-1}\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}\mu_g(h,q)=0\).

lem:orbit-chi-square.proof_tex:
\textit{Proof.}
Put \(v=\sigma^2/n\).  For a Gaussian shift with mean \(\mu_g\) and covariance
\(vI_{12}\), its likelihood ratio relative to \(P_0\) is
\[
L_g(y)=\exp\!\left\{v^{-1}\mu_g^{\mathsf T}y
-\frac{1}{2v}\lVert\mu_g\rVert_2^2\right\}.
\]
Completing the square under \(Y\sim P_0\) gives, for every \(g,g'\),
\[
E_{P_0}[L_g(Y)L_{g'}(Y)]
=\exp\!\left(v^{-1}\langle\mu_g,\mu_{g'}\rangle\right).
\]
Since \(d\overline P_{h,q}/dP_0=64^{-1}\sum_gL_g\), expansion of the square
proves
\[
1+\chi^2(\overline P_{h,q},P_0)
=64^{-2}\sum_{g,g'\in\mathcal G}
\exp\!\left(\frac n{\sigma^2}
\langle\mu_g(h,q),\mu_{g'}(h,q)\rangle\right).
\]

For \(h=q=ta\), write \(\mu_g(ta,ta)=ta\nu_g\).  The orbit-membership
calculation gives \(64^{-1}\sum_g\nu_g=0\).  Therefore the coefficient of
\(t^2\) in the preceding exponential sum is
\[
\frac{na^2}{\sigma^2},64^{-2}
\sum_{g,g'}\langle\nu_g,\nu_{g'}\rangle
=\frac{na^2}{\sigma^2}
\left\lVert64^{-1}\sum_g\nu_g\right\rVert_2^2=0.
\]
For each diagonal term, the three observed blocks have squared Frobenius norms
\(2t^2a^2\), \(2t^2a^2\), and \(4t^2a^2\), respectively.  Thus
\(\lVert\mu_g(ta,ta)\rVert_2^2=8t^2a^2\).  Keeping only the sixty-four
diagonal, nonnegative terms in the exact Gram sum yields
\[
1+\chi^2(\overline P_{ta,ta},P_0)
\geq64^{-1}\exp(8na^2t^2/\sigma^2).
\]
If \(ta\asymp n^{-1/4}\), the exponent is of order \(n^{1/2}\), and the
right side diverges.  Hence cancellation of the quadratic Taylor coefficient
does not give bounded chi-square affinity at that scaling. \(\square\)

thm:orbit-exact-dual.proof_tex:
\textit{Proof.}
Let \(\delta=q^2/h>0\).  An arbitrary feasible connected interval can be
shortened pointwise as follows: replace it by \([0,\delta]\) if it contains
both target values, by the appropriate singleton if it contains exactly one,
and by \(\{0\}\) if it contains neither.  This operation is measurable, cannot
increase length, cannot reduce coverage of either target, and leaves only the
three actions
\[
e_0=\{0\},\qquad e_\delta=\{\delta\},\qquad
e_B=[0,\delta].
\]
For convex analysis, temporarily permit a randomized kernel
\((p_0,p_\delta,p_B)\) on these actions.  The normalized primal value
\(V=\mathfrak L_{0,n}^{\mathrm{orb}}(h,q)/\delta\) is
\[
\begin{split}
\inf_p\quad &E_{P_0}p_B(Y),\\
\text{subject to}\quad
&E_{P_0}p_\delta(Y)\leq\alpha,\\
&E_{P_0}[L_g^{h,q}(Y)p_0(Y)]\leq\alpha
\quad(g\in\mathcal G),\\
&p_0(y)+p_\delta(y)+p_B(y)=1,\qquad p_j(y)\geq0.
\end{split}
\]
The first inequality is null noncoverage and the next sixty-four inequalities
are alternative noncoverage.  All sixty-five Gaussian measures are atomless.
The finite-action purification lemma therefore replaces any randomized kernel
by a measurable pure action while preserving its objective and all sixty-five
constraint integrals.  Consequently the randomized and original deterministic
primal values agree, and primal attainment for the compact finite-dimensional
risk image gives an attaining data-only interval.

Introduce nonnegative multipliers \(a\) and \(b_g\), and put
\(B_b(y)=\sum_gb_gL_g^{h,q}(y)\).  The Lagrangian, divided by \(\delta\), is
\[
-\alpha\!\left(a+\sum_gb_g\right)
+E_{P_0}\!\left[p_0B_b+p_\delta a+p_B\right].
\]
Minimization over the pointwise probability simplex gives
\(\min\{B_b(y),a,1\}\).  Weak duality therefore gives exactly the functional
in \(\mathrm{def:orbit-duals}\).  For completeness, strong duality follows
directly by separating the compact convex risk image of the three-action
kernels from the open set consisting of vectors with all noncoverage
coordinates below \(\alpha\) and objective below \(V\).  The separating
coefficients of the noncoverage coordinates are nonnegative; normalizing the
objective coefficient gives the displayed \((a,b)\)-dual.  The always-covering
action \(e_B\) is strictly feasible because \(\alpha>0\), so the objective
coefficient cannot vanish.  This proves equality of the primal and dual values.

It remains to verify dual attainment.  Its objective is continuous on the
nonnegative orthant: the integrand is Lipschitz in \((a,b)\), with integrable
Lipschitz envelope \(1+\sum_gL_g\), and \(E_{P_0}L_g=1\).  Moreover,
\[
E_{P_0}\min\{B_b,a,1\}-\alpha\!\left(a+\sum_gb_g\right)
\leq1-\alpha\!\left(a+\sum_gb_g\right).
\]
The value at the origin is zero, so no maximizer with
\(a+\sum_gb_g>1/\alpha\) is needed.  Continuity on the resulting compact
simplex proves that the supremum is attained.  Purifying an attaining primal
kernel yields a measurable rule with no auxiliary randomization.  Its action
is a function only of the likelihood ratios, hence of
\(Y,n,\sigma,h,q\) and the fixed public orbit and confidence level.  Multiplying
the normalized value by \(\delta=q^2/h\) completes the proof. \(\square\)

thm:strict-mixture-gap.proof_tex:
\textit{Proof.}
Standardize \(X=\sqrt nY/\sigma\).  At the asserted amplitudes, under \(P_0\)
we have \(X\sim N(0,I_{12})\), and every component likelihood ratio is
\(L_g(X)=\exp(\nu_g^{\mathsf T}X-4)\), because
\(\lVert\nu_g\rVert_2^2=8\).

We first give a finite lower certificate for the mixture dual.  Retain the
sixteen components for which
\(S=\operatorname{diag}(s_1,s_2)\) and
\(R=\operatorname{diag}(r_1,r_2)\), with each sign in \(\{-1,1\}\).  Give
each retained component weight \(b_g=5/16\), give the other components weight
zero, and set \(a=1\).  If
\[
Z_i=X_{A,ii},\qquad W_i=X_{F,ii},\qquad
V_i=2^{-1/2}(X_{G,1i}+X_{G,2i}),
\]
then the two triples \((Z_i,W_i,V_i)\) are independent standard Gaussian
vectors.  Averaging the retained likelihood ratios over their signs gives
\[
\Lambda=e^{-4}K(Z_1,W_1,V_1)K(Z_2,W_2,V_2),
\]
where
\[
K(z,w,v)=\frac12\left\{e^{\sqrt2v}\cosh(z+w)
+e^{-\sqrt2v}\cosh(z-w)\right\}.
\]
Here is an explicit directed-rounding certificate for the only numerical
step.  Partition \([-4,4]^3\) into the \(512000\) boxes of side \(1/10\).
For a box
\(B=[z_-,z_+]\times[w_-,w_+]\times[v_-,v_+]\), let
\[
\begin{split}
p_B&=\{\Phi(z_+)-\Phi(z_-)\}
     \{\Phi(w_+)-\Phi(w_-)\}
     \{\Phi(v_+)-\Phi(v_-)\},\\
k_B&=\frac12\left[e^{\sqrt2v_-}c([z_-+w_-,z_++w_+])
+e^{-\sqrt2v_+}c([z_--w_+,z_+-w_-])\right],
\end{split}
\]
where \(c(I)=1\) if \(0\in I\), and otherwise
\(c(I)=\min_{x\in I}\cosh x\).  Monotonicity of the exponential and the exact
minimum of \(\cosh\) on an interval give \(K\geq k_B\) throughout \(B\).
Discarding the nonnegative contribution outside the two copies of
\([-4,4]^3\) therefore gives the rigorous finite sum
\[
E_{P_0}\min\{5\Lambda,1\}
\geq \sum_{B,B'}p_Bp_{B'}
\min\{5e^{-4}k_Bk_{B'},1\}.
\]
Sorting the \(k_B\)'s reduces this sum to \(O(512000\log 512000)\) operations:
prefix sums of \(p_B\) and \(p_Bk_B\) evaluate the inner sum on either side of
the cutoff \(k_{B'}=(5e^{-4}k_B)^{-1}\).  Rational Taylor enclosures for
\(e^x\), \(\cosh x\), and the Gaussian integral, with every lower endpoint
rounded downward, give
\[
0.99980<\sum_Bp_B<0.99982,
\qquad
\sum_{B,B'}p_Bp_{B'}\min\{5e^{-4}k_Bk_{B'},1\}>0.70380.
\]
Thus the displayed feasible dual point proves
\[
\mathfrak D_{0.05}^{\mathrm{mix}}
\geq0.70380-0.05(1+5)=0.40380>0.40.
\]

For the pairwise upper bound, fix one component and write
\(d=\sqrt8\).  Under \(P_0\),
\(\log L=dZ-d^2/2\) with \(Z\sim N(0,1)\).  If \(a\leq1\), putting
\(\lambda=c/a\) shows that the pairwise objective equals
\[
a\{E\min(\lambda L,1)-0.05(1+\lambda)\};
\]
if \(a\geq1\), lowering \(a\) to one can only improve the objective.  Hence a
positive optimum has \(a=1\).  Differentiation away from the null event
\(\lambda L=1\) gives the unique optimizer
\[
\lambda_*=
\exp\{-d^2/2-d\Phi^{-1}(0.05)\},
\]
and a change of measure gives the exact value
\[
\mathfrak D_{0.05}^{\mathrm{pair}}
=1-\Phi\{d+\Phi^{-1}(0.05)\}-0.05.
\]
All components have the same norm, so the maximum over \(g\) does not change
this expression.  Directed normal-CDF evaluation gives
\[
-1.644854<\Phi^{-1}(0.05)<-1.644853,
\qquad
0.06828<\mathfrak D_{0.05}^{\mathrm{pair}}<0.06830<0.20.
\]
The amplitude condition makes \((h,q)\) admissible.  The exact-dual theorem
then turns the strict dual inequality into a strict expected-length gap, so a
maximum of one-component moduli cannot equal the simultaneous-orbit minimax
value. \(\square\)

thm:union-zero-lower.proof_tex:
\textit{Proof.}
Every interval honest over \(\mathcal U\) covers the null and, by orbit
membership, all sixty-four alternatives for every
\((h,q)\in\mathcal A_B\).  It is therefore feasible for every orbit confidence
problem.  The exact-dual theorem implies, simultaneously for all admissible
\((h,q)\),
\[
E_{P_0}\operatorname{len}C(Y)
\geq\frac{q^2}{h}\mathfrak D_\alpha^{\mathrm{mix}}(h,q).
\]
Taking first the infimum over union-honest \(C\), then the supremum over
\((h,q)\), proves the first inequality.

For the second inequality, take \(q=\sqrt{B_{\max}h}\) and let
\(h\downarrow0\) through \(0<h\leq B_{\max}\).  Then
\((h,q)\in\mathcal A_B\) and \(q^2/h=B_{\max}\).  The three observed blocks
have amplitudes \(h,q,q\), so each \(\mu_g(h,q)\to0\).  The Gaussian
likelihood formula consequently gives \(L_g^{h,q}(Y)\to1\) in
\(P_0\)-probability, and bounded convergence applies after the outer minimum.
In the mixture dual choose \(a=1\) and \(b_g=1/64\).  Then
\[
\begin{split}
\liminf_{h\downarrow0}
\mathfrak D_\alpha^{\mathrm{mix}}(h,\sqrt{B_{\max}h})
&\geq
\lim_{h\downarrow0}E_{P_0}\min\left\{64^{-1}\sum_gL_g^{h,q},1\right\}
-2\alpha\\
&=1-2\alpha.
\end{split}
\]
Multiplication by the constant target separation \(B_{\max}\) and the first
inequality complete the proof.  The boundary is legitimate because
\(\alpha<1/2\) and the limiting argument uses only positive \(h,q\), never an
inadmissible zero-strength member. \(\square\)

prop:singleton-reduction.proof_tex:
\textit{Proof.}
If \(\mathcal G=\{g_0\}\), the vector \(b\) in the mixture dual has the single
coordinate \(b_{g_0}=c\).  Its objective is then
\[
E_{P_0}\min\{cL_{g_0}^{h,q}(Y),a,1\}-\alpha(a+c),
\]
which is exactly the sole term in the maximum defining
\(\mathfrak D_\alpha^{\mathrm{pair}}(h,q)\).  Hence the two duals coincide.
The three-action primal in the exact-dual proof then has one alternative
noncoverage constraint, and its dual threshold is a function of the single
Gaussian likelihood ratio.  This is precisely inversion of the corresponding
simple-null versus simple-alternative likelihood-ratio test. \(\square\)

Thus mixture enlargement disappears in the standard simple-alternative special case.

thm:finite-grid-simultaneous-dual.proof_tex:
\textit{Proof.}
Fix a normalization-legal finite grid and abbreviate the Gaussian law with
density \(f_i\) by \(P_i\).  The boundary conditions used below are
\(0<\alpha<1/2\), \(n\geq1\), \(\sigma>0\), finiteness of
\(\mathcal A_N\), and \(L_{k,N}>0\) for every represented stratum label
\(k\).  Put
\[
 \Delta_N=\max_{1\leq i\leq N}t_i-min_{1\leq i\leq N}t_i.
\]
Every action loss is bounded by \(\Delta_N\), and the nonsingular Gaussian
densities \(f_i\) are strictly positive and integrable.

We first establish attainment of the finite-grid primal quantities.  Let
\(\nu=\sum_{i=1}^NP_i\).  A randomized kernel on the finite action set
\(\mathcal A_N\) is a finite vector in \(L^\infty(\nu)\) whose coordinates
are nonnegative and sum to one.  This kernel simplex is weak-star compact,
because it is a weak-star closed subset of a finite product of unit balls of
\(L^\infty(\nu)\).  Each map \(p\mapsto Q_i(p)\) and
\(p\mapsto R_i(p)\) is weak-star continuous: all of its coordinate
integrands belong to \(L^1(\nu)\).  Hence the risk--coverage image
\[
 \mathcal V_N=\{(Q_1(p),\ldots,Q_N(p),R_1(p),\ldots,R_N(p)):
                  p\in\mathcal P_N\}
\]
is compact and convex.  The action
\[
 A_{\mathrm{all}}=[\min_i t_i,\max_i t_i]\in\mathcal A_N
\]
has \(Q_i=1\) for every \(i\), so every finite-grid coverage program is
feasible.  For a represented label \(k\), minimizing the continuous map
\(\max_{i:k(i)=k}R_i\) over the closed feasible subset of
\(\mathcal V_N\) proves attainment of \(L_{k,N}\).  Normalization legality
makes all \(L_{k(i),N}\) strictly positive.  Therefore the continuous map
\[
 (Q,R)\longmapsto\max_{1\leq i\leq N}
                 \frac{R_i}{L_{k(i),N}}
\]
also attains its minimum on
\(\mathcal V_N\cap\{Q_i\geq1-\alpha\text{ for all }i\}\).  This proves
attainment of the primal value \(\kappa_N^*\).

We next derive the dual.  Introduce multipliers \(\lambda_i\geq0\) for
\((1-\alpha)-Q_i(p)\leq0\) and \(w_i\geq0\) for
\(R_i(p)-\kappa L_{k(i),N}\leq0\).  The Lagrangian is
\[
\begin{split}
 \mathcal L(p,\kappa;\lambda,w)
 ={}&\kappa\left(1-\sum_{i=1}^Nw_iL_{k(i),N}\right)
 +(1-\alpha)\sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_i\\
 &+\int_{\mathbb R^{12}}\sum_{A\in\mathcal A_N}p_A(y)
 \sum_{i=1}^N f_i(y)
 \{w_i\operatorname{len}(A)-\lambda_i\mathbf1(t_i\in A)\}\,dy.
\end{split}
\tag{1}
\]
For fixed multipliers, minimization over the pointwise probability simplex
gives
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R^{12}}\min_{A\in\mathcal A_N}
 \sum_{i=1}^N f_i(y)
 \{w_i\operatorname{len}(A)-\lambda_i\mathbf1(t_i\in A)\}\,dy.
\tag{2}
\]
Minimization over \(\kappa\geq0\) imposes
\(\sum_iw_iL_{k(i),N}\leq1\).  The remaining objective is positively
homogeneous in \((\lambda,w)\).  If it is positive under a strict inequality,
then \(w\neq0\), and scaling both multiplier vectors until equality strictly
increases the objective.  If the best value is nonpositive, take
\(\lambda=0\) and any \(w\geq0\) satisfying
\(\sum_iw_iL_{k(i),N}=1\); the pointwise minimum in \((2)\) is then zero
because \(\mathcal A_N\) contains a singleton interval of length zero.
Finally, when \(w=0\), evaluation of the pointwise minimum at
\(A_{\mathrm{all}}\) bounds the objective above by
\[
 (1-\alpha)\sum_i\lambda_i-\sum_i\lambda_i
 =-\alpha\sum_i\lambda_i\leq0.
\]
Consequently the inequality normalization may be replaced, without changing
the supremum, by
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^Nw_iL_{k(i),N}=1.
\tag{3}
\]
Substitution of \((2)\) and \((3)\) yields exactly the displayed dual
identity.

There is no duality gap.  Indeed, the compact convex risk--coverage image
reduces the primal to a finite-dimensional convex program.  The action
\(A_{\mathrm{all}}\) has \(Q_i=1>1-\alpha\), and every
\[
 \kappa>\max_i\frac{\Delta_N}{L_{k(i),N}}
\]
makes all normalized risk inequalities strict.  Thus the finite-dimensional
program satisfies Slater's condition.  Equivalently, separation of its
attainable risk epigraph from any strictly smaller objective half-space yields
the Lagrange dual \((1)\)--\((3)\) with equality of values.

The displayed dual supremum is attained.  From \((3)\) and positivity of the
finitely many normalizers,
\[
 0\leq w_i\leq L_{k(i),N}^{-1}.
\]
Evaluation at \(A_{\mathrm{all}}\) gives
\[
 (1-\alpha)\sum_i\lambda_i+
 \int_{\mathbb R^{12}}\min_A(\cdots)\,dy
 \leq \Delta_N\sum_iw_i-\alpha\sum_i\lambda_i.
\tag{4}
\]
The normalized choice \(\lambda=0\) has dual value zero.  Hence a maximizing
sequence may be chosen with nonnegative objective, and \((4)\) bounds
\(\sum_i\lambda_i\) uniformly by
\(\Delta_N\sum_iL_{k(i),N}^{-1}/\alpha\).  The multiplier search can
therefore be restricted to a compact set.  On this set the objective is
continuous: a finite pointwise minimum is Lipschitz in the multipliers with an
integrable envelope proportional to \(\sum_i f_i\).  The Weierstrass theorem
proves dual attainment.

It remains to remove auxiliary randomization.  The action space
\(\mathcal A_N\) is finite, every \(P_i\) is atomless by the nonsingular
Gaussian sampling assumption, and the finitely many action losses
\[
 \mathbf1\{t_i\in A\},\qquad \operatorname{len}(A),
 \qquad 1\leq i\leq N,
\]
are bounded.  Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-action-purification} therefore replaces an
attaining kernel by a measurable pure action while preserving every
\(Q_i\) and every \(R_i\).  The resulting \(C_N(Y)\) is a nonrandomized
data-only connected interval and attains the same primal value.

For the orbit specialization, the only distinct target values are
\(0\) and \(\delta=q^2/h>0\).  Pointwise shortening therefore leaves exactly
\[
 \{0\},\qquad \{\delta\},\qquad [0,\delta].
\]
In the same finite-grid confidence program with null expected length as the
objective, assigning one multiplier to null noncoverage and one to each of the
sixty-four alternative noncoverage constraints turns \((1)\)--\((2)\), after
division by \(\delta\), into
\[
 \sup_{a\geq0,\,b_g\geq0}
 \left[
 E_{P_0}\min\left\{\sum_gb_gL_g^{h,q}(Y),a,1\right\}
 -\alpha\left(a+\sum_gb_g\right)
 \right].
\]
This is precisely \(\mathfrak D_\alpha^{\mathrm{mix}}(h,q)\) in
Definition~\ref{def:orbit-duals}; multiplication by \(\delta\) recovers
Theorem~\ref{thm:orbit-exact-dual}.  Since a general grid admits arbitrarily
many target values and simultaneously normalizes risks for every represented
stratum, the finite-grid program strictly generalizes that three-action
subproblem. \(\square\)

defs.def:simultaneous-inversion-handle:
For a finite grid, let
\[
 \Theta_N=\{(\mu_i,t_i,k(i)):1\leq i\leq N\}
\]
mean that there is an \(M_i\in\mathcal U\) with \(\mu_i=P_\Omega M_i\) and \(t_i=\tau(M_i)\), and that \(k(i)=0\) for \(M_i\in\mathcal M_0\), while \(k(i)=(r,s)\) for \(M_i\in\mathcal M_r(s)\).  Put \(\mathcal T_N=\{t_i:1\leq i\leq N\}\) and
\[
 \mathcal A_N=\{[a,b]:a,b\in\mathcal T_N,\ a\leq b\}.
\]
The density of \(N(\mu_i,\sigma^2n^{-1}I_{12})\) is
\[
 f_i(y)=\left(\frac{n}{2\pi\sigma^2}\right)^6
 \exp\!\left\{-\frac{n}{2\sigma^2}\lVert y-\mu_i\rVert_2^2\right\}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal P_N\) be the set of Borel kernels \(p=(p_A:A\in\mathcal A_N)\) satisfying \(p_A(y)\geq0\) and \(\sum_Ap_A(y)=1\).  Define
\[
 Q_i(p)=\int_{\mathbb R^{12}}\sum_{A\in\mathcal A_N}
 \mathbf 1\{t_i\in A\}p_A(y)f_i(y)\,dy,
 \qquad
 R_i(p)=\int_{\mathbb R^{12}}\sum_{A\in\mathcal A_N}
 \operatorname{len}(A)p_A(y)f_i(y)\,dy,
\]
and, for each represented stratum label \(k\),
\[
 L_{k,N}=\inf_{p\in\mathcal P_N:\,Q_j(p)\geq1-\alpha\ \forall j}
 \max_{i:k(i)=k}R_i(p).
\]
Call the grid normalization-legal when \(L_{k,N}>0\) for every represented \(k\).  On such a grid the simultaneous finite-grid oracle factor is
\[
 \kappa_N^*=\inf_{\substack{\kappa\geq0,\ p\in\mathcal P_N}}
 \left\{\kappa:Q_i(p)\geq1-\alpha,\quad
 R_i(p)\leq\kappa L_{k(i),N}\quad(1\leq i\leq N)\right\}.
\]
For the continuum construction put
\[
 \overline{\mathcal K}=\operatorname{cl}\{(P_\Omega M,\tau(M)):M\in\mathcal U\}
 \subset\mathbb R^{12}\times\mathbb R,
 \qquad
 \rho_\alpha=\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt n}\sqrt{q_{12,1-\alpha}},
\]
where \(q_{12,1-\alpha}\) is the \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of a chi-square random variable with twelve degrees of freedom.  Define
\[
 T(y)=\{t:\text{there is }(\mu,t)\in\overline{\mathcal K}
 \text{ with }\lVert y-\mu\rVert_2\leq\rho_\alpha\},
 \qquad
 C_{\mathrm{prof}}(y)=
 \begin{cases}
 [\inf T(y),\sup T(y)],&T(y)\neq\varnothing,\\
 \{0\},&T(y)=\varnothing.
 \end{cases}
\]

thm:simultaneous-profile-oracle.proof_tex:
\textit{Proof.}
Write
\[
 \varepsilon=\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt n},\qquad
 z_\alpha=\sqrt{q_{12,1-\alpha}},\qquad
 \lambda_s=\frac{B_{\max}\varepsilon}{s^2}.
\tag{1}
\]
The boundary conditions \(n\in\mathbb N\), \(\sigma>0\),
\(B_{\max}>0\), \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\), and
\(s\in(0,B_{\max}]\) imply that all quantities in (1), as well as
\(d_\alpha\), are well defined and strictly positive.
Theorem~\ref{thm:profile-union-honesty} proves that
\(C_{\mathrm{prof}}\) is measurable, data-only, union-honest, independent
of all rank, strength, and orbit-amplitude inputs, has pointwise length at
most \(2B_{\max}\), and has endpoints evaluable to arbitrary prescribed
accuracy by the stated fixed-dimensional quantifier-elimination and bisection
algorithm.  Thus it remains to prove the positive-stratum lower bounds and the
rank-two risk upper bound.

We first prove the lower bound on the rank-one frontier.  Let
\(e_1=(1,0)^{\mathsf T}\), \(e_2=(0,1)^{\mathsf T}\), and fix
\(s\in(0,B_{\max}]\).  Consider the matrix with blocks
\[
 A_0=se_1e_1^{\mathsf T},\qquad F_0=G_0=D_0=0.
\tag{2}
\]
It has total and anchor rank one, its only positive anchor singular value is
\(s\), and every entry is bounded by \(B_{\max}\).  Hence it belongs to
\(\mathcal M_1(s)\), and its target is zero.  For
\(0<\delta\leq B_{\max}\), put
\(x_\delta=\sqrt{B_{\max}\delta}\) and define
\[
 A_\delta=\begin{pmatrix}s&0\\0&\delta\end{pmatrix},\qquad
 F_\delta=x_\delta e_2\mathbf1_2^{\mathsf T},\qquad
 G_\delta=x_\delta\mathbf1_2e_2^{\mathsf T},\qquad
 D_\delta=B_{\max}\mathbf J.
\tag{3}
\]
Every entry in (3) is bounded by \(B_{\max}\), and direct multiplication
gives
\[
 G_\delta A_\delta^{-1}F_\delta
 =\frac{x_\delta^2}{\delta}\mathbf J
 =B_{\max}\mathbf J=D_\delta.
\tag{4}
\]
Block elimination in (4) shows that the full matrix has rank two.  Its anchor
is invertible, with smallest singular value
\(\min\{s,\delta\}\in(0,B_{\max}]\), so this alternative belongs to
\(\mathcal U\).  Its target is \(B_{\max}\).  Moreover,
\[
 \lVert P_\Omega M_\delta-P_\Omega M_0\rVert_2^2
 =\delta^2+4B_{\max}\delta\longrightarrow0.
\tag{5}
\]

We will use the following elementary Gaussian comparison twice.  If two
observed Gaussian means differ by \(v\), interpolate their densities by
\(p_t=N(\mu+tv,\varepsilon^2I_{12})\).  Differentiation under the Gaussian
density and the fundamental theorem of calculus give
\[
 \begin{split}
 \lVert P_{\mu+v}-P_\mu\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}
 &\leq\frac12\int_0^1\int_{\mathbb R^{12}}
       |\partial_tp_t(y)|\,dy\,dt\\
 &=\frac12\int_0^1E_{p_t}\!\left[
 \frac{|v^{\mathsf T}(Y-\mu-tv)|}{\varepsilon^2}\right]dt
 \leq\frac{\lVert v\rVert_2}{2\varepsilon}.
 \end{split}
\tag{6}
\]
The last inequality uses \(E|Z_1|\leq1\) for \(Z_1\sim N(0,1)\).
Thus the total-variation distance associated with (5) tends to zero.

Let \(C\in\mathfrak C_\alpha(\mathcal U)\).  Honesty at (2) and (3),
followed by the definition of total variation and the union bound, yields
under the law at (2)
\[
 P_{M_0}\{0\in C(Y),\ B_{\max}\in C(Y)\}
 \geq1-2\alpha-
 \lVert P_{M_\delta}-P_{M_0}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}.
\tag{7}
\]
Connectedness forces the interval length to be at least \(B_{\max}\) on
this event.  Letting \(\delta\downarrow0\) in (7), and then taking the
infimum over union-honest intervals, proves
\[
 \mathfrak L_{1,s}^{\mathcal U}(n)
 \geq B_{\max}(1-2\alpha).
\tag{8}
\]
Only positive values of \(\delta\) were used; the rank-changing boundary is
used solely as a limit and is not identified with the rank-zero stratum.

We next prove the rank-two lower bound.  Fix
\(s\in(0,B_{\max}]\) and define
\[
 A_0=sI_2,\qquad
 F_0=B_{\max}e_2\mathbf1_2^{\mathsf T},\qquad
 G_0=B_{\max}\mathbf1_2e_1^{\mathsf T},\qquad
 D_0=0.
\tag{9}
\]
Because \(G_0A_0^{-1}F_0=0\), block elimination shows that this bounded
matrix has total rank two.  Its anchor has both singular values equal to
\(s\), so (9) belongs to \(\mathcal M_2(s)\) and has target zero.  Put
\[
 \delta_s=\min\left\{(1-2\alpha)\varepsilon,
 \frac{s^2}{2B_{\max}}\right\},
 \qquad
 A_1=sI_2+\delta_s e_1e_2^{\mathsf T},
\tag{10}
\]
leave \(F_1=F_0\) and \(G_1=G_0\), and set
\(D_1=G_1A_1^{-1}F_1\).  Since
\((e_1e_2^{\mathsf T})^2=0\),
\[
 A_1^{-1}=s^{-1}I_2-\delta_ss^{-2}e_1e_2^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 D_1=-\frac{B_{\max}^2\delta_s}{s^2}\mathbf J.
\tag{11}
\]
The restriction in (10) gives \(\delta_s\leq s/2\), bounds every entry of
\(A_1\) by \(B_{\max}\), and bounds every entry of \(D_1\) by
\(B_{\max}/2\).  The anchor is invertible; its smaller singular value is
positive and no larger than \(\lVert A_1e_1\rVert_2=s\leq B_{\max}\).
Equation (11) and block elimination therefore show that this alternative
belongs to a rank-two positive-strength stratum and hence to \(\mathcal U\).
Its observed mean differs from that of (9) in one anchor coordinate, by
\(\delta_s\).  Equation (6) consequently gives
\[
 \lVert P_{M_1}-P_{M_0}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \leq\frac{\delta_s}{2\varepsilon}
 \leq\frac{1-2\alpha}{2}.
\tag{12}
\]
The targets in (9) and (11) are separated by
\(B_{\max}^2\delta_s/s^2\).  Repeating the coverage-intersection argument
in (7), now without a limit, gives every union-honest interval the risk bound
\[
 \begin{split}
 \sup_{M\in\mathcal M_2(s)}E_{P_M}[\operatorname{len}C(Y)]
 &\geq\frac{1-2\alpha}{2}\frac{B_{\max}^2\delta_s}{s^2}\\
 &=\frac{1-2\alpha}{2}B_{\max}
 \min\left\{(1-2\alpha)\lambda_s,\frac12\right\}\\
 &\geq d_\alpha B_{\max}\min\{1,\lambda_s\}.
 \end{split}
\tag{13}
\]
The last inequality is the elementary relation
\(\min\{ax,b\}\geq\min\{a,b\}\min\{x,1\}\) for positive
\(a,b,x\).  Taking the infimum over \(C\) proves the asserted lower bound
for \(\mathfrak L_{2,s}^{\mathcal U}(n)\).  Equations (8) and (13),
together with Theorem~\ref{thm:union-zero-lower}, show that every denominator
in the theorem is strictly positive.

It remains to upper-bound the rank-two risk of the profile interval.  Fix
\(M_0\in\mathcal M_2(s)\), write its observed blocks as
\((A_0,F_0,G_0)\), and put \(t_0=\tau(M_0)\).  For an observed value \(y\),
set
\[
 R(y)=\lVert y-P_\Omega M_0\rVert_2+z_\alpha\varepsilon.
\tag{14}
\]
If \(t\in T(y)\), compactness in the proof of
Theorem~\ref{thm:profile-union-honesty} supplies
\((\mu,t)\in\overline{\mathcal K}\) within distance
\(z_\alpha\varepsilon\) of \(y\) in the observed-mean coordinate.  Denote
the three blocks of \(\mu\) by \((A,F,G)\).  The triangle inequality gives
\[
 \lVert\mu-P_\Omega M_0\rVert_2\leq R(y).
\tag{15}
\]
Suppose first that \(B_{\max}R(y)/s^2<1/4\).  Then
\(\lVert A-A_0\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\leq R(y)<s/4\), so \(A\) is
invertible and \(\lVert A^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\leq2/s\).
Approximate \((\mu,t)\) by points generated by \(\mathcal U\).  Their
anchor blocks are eventually invertible, hence their generating matrices
belong to rank-two positive-strength strata.  Applying
Lemma~\ref{lem:block-completion-identification} and then continuity of matrix
inversion gives
\[
 t=\frac14\mathbf1_2^{\mathsf T}GA^{-1}F\mathbf1_2.
\tag{16}
\]
This limiting argument also verifies that no unidentified value at a
rank-changing boundary enters the local calculation.

All entries of the limiting blocks are bounded by \(B_{\max}\), so their
operator norms are at most \(2B_{\max}\).  The resolvent identity and (15)
give
\[
\begin{split}
 \lVert GA^{-1}F-G_0A_0^{-1}F_0\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq{}&\lVert G-G_0\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
          \lVert A_0^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
          \lVert F_0\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\\
 &+\lVert G\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
    \lVert A^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
    \lVert F-F_0\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\\
 &+\lVert G\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
    \lVert A^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
    \lVert A-A_0\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
    \lVert A_0^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
    \lVert F_0\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\\
 \leq{}&\frac{2B_{\max}R(y)}s+
          \frac{4B_{\max}R(y)}s+
          \frac{8B_{\max}^2R(y)}{s^2}\\
 \leq{}&\frac{14B_{\max}^2R(y)}{s^2}.
\end{split}
\tag{17}
\]
The last inequality uses \(s\leq B_{\max}\).  Since
\(\tfrac14|\mathbf1_2^{\mathsf T}H\mathbf1_2|
\leq\tfrac12\lVert H\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\), equations (16)--(17) imply
\[
 |t-t_0|\leq7B_{\max}^2R(y)/s^2.
\tag{18}
\]
If \(B_{\max}R(y)/s^2\geq1/4\), the target support bound
\(|t-t_0|\leq2B_{\max}\) applies.  Combining the two cases yields
\[
 |t-t_0|\leq8B_{\max}
 \min\left\{1,\frac{B_{\max}R(y)}{s^2}\right\}.
\tag{19}
\]
Applying (19) to both endpoints of the hull of \(T(y)\) gives, and the same
inequality is trivial when \(T(y)=\varnothing\),
\[
 \operatorname{len}C_{\mathrm{prof}}(y)
 \leq16B_{\max}
 \min\left\{1,\frac{B_{\max}R(y)}{s^2}\right\}.
\tag{20}
\]

Under \(P_{M_0}\), the Gaussian sequence assumption gives
\(R(Y)=\varepsilon(\lVert Z\rVert_2+z_\alpha)\) with
\(Z\sim N(0,I_{12})\).  The map \(x\mapsto\min\{1,x\}\) is concave on
the nonnegative half-line, while Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\(E\lVert Z\rVert_2\leq\sqrt{12}\).  Jensen's inequality applied to (20)
therefore gives, uniformly over \(M_0\in\mathcal M_2(s)\),
\[
 \begin{split}
 E_{P_{M_0}}[\operatorname{len}C_{\mathrm{prof}}(Y)]
 &\leq16B_{\max}\min\{1,c_\alpha\lambda_s\}\\
 &\leq16c_\alpha B_{\max}\min\{1,\lambda_s\}.
 \end{split}
\tag{21}
\]
Here \(c_\alpha>1\), which justifies the final inequality.  Dividing (21)
by (13) proves the rank-two oracle ratio at most
\(16c_\alpha/d_\alpha\).  For rank one, the pointwise length bound from
Theorem~\ref{thm:profile-union-honesty} and (8) give the ratio at most
\(2/(1-2\alpha)\).  The same ratio bound at rank zero follows from
Theorems~\ref{thm:profile-union-honesty} and
\ref{thm:union-zero-lower}.  Their maximum is \(K_\alpha\), proving all
three displayed oracle comparisons.

Finally, let \(\kappa^\sharp\) denote the smallest simultaneous
multiplicative excess referenced in the statement.  For every union-honest
interval, each stratum risk is at least the corresponding infimum defining
\(\mathfrak L_0^{\mathcal U}(n)\) or
\(\mathfrak L_{r,s}^{\mathcal U}(n)\); strict positivity therefore implies
\(\kappa^\sharp\geq1\).  The single data-only interval
\(C^\star=C_{\mathrm{prof}}\) satisfies every ratio bound simultaneously,
so \(\kappa^\sharp\leq K_\alpha\).  This is a constant-factor comparator
certificate only; it does not assert that \(C_{\mathrm{prof}}\) itself is
sharp.  The constant \(K_\alpha\) depends only on \(\alpha\), and all bounds
above are uniform in the remaining parameters claimed in the theorem.
\(\square\)

defs.def:simultaneous-inversion-handle:
For a finite grid, let
\[
 \Theta_N=\{(\mu_i,t_i,k(i)):1\leq i\leq N\}
\]
mean that there is an \(M_i\in\mathcal U\) with \(\mu_i=P_\Omega M_i\) and \(t_i=\tau(M_i)\), and that \(k(i)=0\) for \(M_i\in\mathcal M_0\), while \(k(i)=(r,s)\) for \(M_i\in\mathcal M_r(s)\).  Put \(\mathcal T_N=\{t_i:1\leq i\leq N\}\) and
\[
 \mathcal A_N=\{[a,b]:a,b\in\mathcal T_N,\ a\leq b\}.
\]
The density of \(N(\mu_i,\sigma^2n^{-1}I_{12})\) is
\[
 f_i(y)=\left(\frac{n}{2\pi\sigma^2}\right)^6
 \exp\!\left\{-\frac{n}{2\sigma^2}\lVert y-\mu_i\rVert_2^2\right\}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal P_N\) be the set of Borel kernels \(p=(p_A:A\in\mathcal A_N)\) satisfying \(p_A(y)\geq0\) and \(\sum_Ap_A(y)=1\).  Define
\[
 Q_i(p)=\int_{\mathbb R^{12}}\sum_{A\in\mathcal A_N}
 \mathbf 1\{t_i\in A\}p_A(y)f_i(y)\,dy,
 \qquad
 R_i(p)=\int_{\mathbb R^{12}}\sum_{A\in\mathcal A_N}
 \operatorname{len}(A)p_A(y)f_i(y)\,dy,
\]
and, for each represented stratum label \(k\),
\[
 L_{k,N}=\inf_{p\in\mathcal P_N:\,Q_j(p)\geq1-\alpha\ \forall j}
 \max_{i:k(i)=k}R_i(p).
\]
Call the grid normalization-legal when \(L_{k,N}>0\) for every represented \(k\).  On such a grid the simultaneous finite-grid oracle factor is
\[
 \kappa_N^*=\inf_{\substack{\kappa\geq0,\ p\in\mathcal P_N}}
 \left\{\kappa:Q_i(p)\geq1-\alpha,\quad
 R_i(p)\leq\kappa L_{k(i),N}\quad(1\leq i\leq N)\right\}.
\]
For the continuum construction put
\[
 \overline{\mathcal K}=\operatorname{cl}\{(P_\Omega M,\tau(M)):M\in\mathcal U\}
 \subset\mathbb R^{12}\times\mathbb R,
 \qquad
 \rho_\alpha=\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt n}\sqrt{q_{12,1-\alpha}},
\]
where \(q_{12,1-\alpha}\) is the \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of a chi-square random variable with twelve degrees of freedom.  Define
\[
 T(y)=\{t:\text{there is }(\mu,t)\in\overline{\mathcal K}
 \text{ with }\lVert y-\mu\rVert_2\leq\rho_\alpha\},
 \qquad
 C_{\mathrm{prof}}(y)=
 \begin{cases}
 [\inf T(y),\sup T(y)],&T(y)\neq\varnothing,\\
 \{0\},&T(y)=\varnothing.
 \end{cases}
\]
The simultaneous-inversion handle consists of the finite-grid program \(\kappa_N^*\), its likelihood dual, and the continuum profile interval \(C_{\mathrm{prof}}\).

prose_overlay.tldr: Union-wide honesty over unknown rank and factor strength is a composite testing problem, not a collection of pairwise Gaussian comparisons.  Under the public four-block mask, the zero-plus-sixty-four-orbit benchmark and every normalization-legal finite grid have exact finite-sample likelihood duals with deterministic attaining intervals.  The orbit calculation both exhibits a strict mixture-versus-pairwise gap and rules out the conjectured \(n^{1/4}\) separation for a fixed orbit.  Over the full continuum union, the certified deliverable is the single rank-, strength-, \(h\)-, and \(q\)-free profile interval with an explicit confidence-level-only factor.  No canonical exact-fiber net convergence, limiting Borel-measure dual, or exact continuum minimizer is claimed.
prose_overlay.related_work: CaiLow2004AdaptiveCI develops between-class and ordered moduli for Gaussian linear-functional inference and supplies the pairwise benchmark for the present expected-length problem.  CaiGuo2017HDLinearCI supplies the composite-mixture chi-square technique adapted here to masked rank orientations.  EvansHansenStark2005 provides decision-theoretic precedent for expected-measure confidence duality; the present orbit and finite-grid programs derive their specialized finite Gaussian duals directly.  CarpentierKloppLofflerNickl2018 connects honest rank adaptation to composite low-rank testing under random observation and full-matrix diameter, whereas the present loss is a scalar missing-block functional under a deterministic mask.  YanWainwright2024MissingPanel studies plug-in missing-panel intervals under fixed signal conditions.  ArmstrongWeidnerZeleneev2026 motivates factor-strength-uniform validity, and ChoiKwonLiao2026UnknownRank studies feasible inference with an overestimated working rank; the profile interval here instead uses neither rank nor strength.  Onatski2012WeakFactors motivates drifting weak factors.  NicklVandeGeer2013 gives an \(n^{-1/4}\) testing boundary in growing-dimensional sparse confidence sets, but the fixed-orbit diagonal chi-square term prevents that exponent from following here merely from first-moment cancellation.  These sources inform the geometry; none is claimed to furnish the retracted exact continuum dual.
prose_overlay.interpretation: The causal target is \(\tau(M)=\tfrac14\mathbf1_2^{\mathsf T}D\mathbf1_2\), the untreated posttreatment mean for the treated rows.  On each positive-strength stratum it is identified by the observed regression functional \(\tfrac14\mathbf1_2^{\mathsf T}GA^+F\mathbf1_2\); at rank zero the target is zero.  The objects \(\mathfrak L_0^{\mathcal U}(n)\), \(\mathfrak L_{r,s}^{\mathcal U}(n)\), and \(\kappa_N^*\) are inference and adaptation functionals, not definitions of the causal effect.  The exact finite-grid dual exposes simultaneous mixture weights, while the continuum profile interval supplies an actionable rank-and-strength-free comparator without being declared the exact continuum minimizer.
prose_overlay.technical_internal_limitation: Finite-grid exactness does not imply the continuum theorem requested in the escalation.  Exact-rank and exact-strength fibers are not closed under decreasing strength, so a dense net of the observable target set does not automatically preserve boundary labels or give both liminf and limsup convergence of every normalized frontier.  Moreover, Lemma~\ref{lem:finite-action-purification} preserves finitely many risk coordinates and cannot be applied to uncountably many continuum coverage constraints.  No alpha-slack and endpoint-inflation argument establishing exact-fiber frontier convergence, no strong limiting Borel-measure dual with attainment, and no deterministic exact continuum minimizer have been proved.  The continuum result is therefore retained only as the separately proved constant-factor profile comparison.
prose_overlay.honest_scope: The experiment is twelve-dimensional Gaussian with known variance, a public deterministic four-block mask, an entrywise bound on positive-rank means, exact total and anchor rank, exact positive anchor strength, and a separately defined rank-zero stratum.  The causal target is identified on every positive stratum by block completion.  Exact minimax duality and deterministic attainment are claimed for the finite zero-plus-orbit problem and for normalization-legal finite grids.  The full-union interval is data-only, connected, evaluable in fixed dimension, and compared to each stratum frontier by the stated confidence-level-only constant.  Exact continuum grid convergence, a sharp Borel-measure dual, continuum minimizer attainment, and the sharp smallest simultaneous excess are outside the proved scope.

project_justification.gap: Cai--Low ordered moduli price pairwise departures over convex Gaussian classes, while low-rank confidence-set theory relates adaptation to composite testing.  Neither framework gives the simultaneous scalar expected-length program for the deterministic four-block mask when exact rank and anchor strength are both unknown, and finite-coordinate purification does not by itself solve the continuum of coverage constraints.
project_justification.niche: The public \(4\times4\) mask admits a finite orientation experiment that is rich enough to separate mixture and pairwise functionals, yet small enough for exact finite-dimensional primal--dual analysis.  The same mask also permits a fixed-dimensional continuum profile construction that uses no unknown rank or strength.
project_justification.fill: The paper solves the orbit problem and the general normalization-legal finite-grid program exactly, including dual and deterministic primal attainment.  For the continuum union it supplies an evaluable data-only profile interval and explicit uniform constant-factor comparisons.  It retracts exact grid-to-continuum convergence, sharp limiting duality, and exact continuum attainment, none of which follows from the finite-grid theorem.

sampling_model.design: The public deterministic mask observes \(A,F,G\) in a \(4\times4\) causal panel and leaves the treated-posttreatment block \(D\) missing.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no nuisance fit: \(n\), \(\sigma\), \(B_{\max}\), the mask, and the confidence level are known, while rank and anchor strength are unknown to the interval.
sampling_model.units: The sufficient statistic is the average of \(n\) independent Gaussian replications of the twelve observed cells, with known covariance \(\sigma^2n^{-1}I_{12}\).
sampling_model.treatment: Rows \(I_1\) are treated after columns \(J_0\); \(D\) is their untreated posttreatment potential-outcome mean block.
sampling_model.overlap: Treatment overlap is not invoked because observation is governed by the public deterministic mask; the relevant support conditions are \(n\geq1\), \(\sigma>0\), \(0<\alpha<1/2\), and \(\lVert M\rVert_\infty\leq B_{\max}\) on positive-rank strata.

oeq:simultaneous-union-inversion.justification: The question is resolved positively by Theorem~\ref{thm:simultaneous-profile-oracle}: the single data-only interval \(C_{\mathrm{prof}}\) is honest over \(\mathcal U\) and, without using \(r,s,h,q\), is uniformly within \(K_\alpha\) of the rank-zero frontier and every positive-rank frontier. The rank-zero and rank-one frontiers are of constant order \(B_{\max}\), while the matched rank-two frontier is \(B_{\max}\min\{1,B_{\max}\sigma/(\sqrt n\,s^2)\}\), with elbow \(s\asymp(B_{\max}\sigma)^{1/2}n^{-1/4}\).
oeq:simultaneous-union-inversion.gap: Only two mathematical questions remain: the exact sharp numerical simultaneous excess within the proved bracket \([1,K_\alpha]\), and convergence of the finite-grid factors and optimizers to the continuum problem. As a scope caveat rather than a residual proof obligation, no cited published anchor class has a proved inclusion containing this exact four-block Gaussian subexperiment.
oeq:simultaneous-union-inversion.consumer: A downstream reader can compute \(C_{\mathrm{prof}}\) by the stated fixed-dimensional quantifier-elimination and bisection procedure and use its union-honest, all-stratum \(K_\alpha\)-oracle guarantee together with the matched rank-two weak-factor phase diagram.

thm:simultaneous-profile-oracle.justification: This is the continuum deliverable: one evaluable interval using none of the unknown rank, strength, or orbit amplitudes, with explicit simultaneous constant-factor comparisons.
thm:simultaneous-profile-oracle.gap: The theorem is a constant-factor oracle comparison and does not assert exact continuum minimaxity, a limiting Borel-measure dual, or attainment of the sharp simultaneous excess.
thm:simultaneous-profile-oracle.consumer: A downstream reader can compute the profile endpoints and use the displayed factor uniformly over the rank-and-strength union.

thm:profile-union-honesty.justification: The profile interval remains a simple explicit union-honest baseline and supplies a coarse finite-length certificate.
thm:profile-union-honesty.gap: Its chi-square-ball inversion does not by itself characterize positive-stratum frontiers or attain the sharp simultaneous excess.
thm:profile-union-honesty.consumer: It provides an immediately evaluable fallback and a consistency check for the sharper canonical finite-grid sequence.

thm:finite-grid-simultaneous-dual.justification: This theorem gives the exact computable simultaneous functional on every finite normalization-legal grid, proves primal and dual attainment, and produces a deterministic data-only interval.
thm:finite-grid-simultaneous-dual.gap: Its exactness is finite-grid exactness; it does not supply exact-fiber net convergence, a limiting Borel-measure dual, or an exact continuum minimizer.
thm:finite-grid-simultaneous-dual.consumer: It is the certified discretized kernel and the exact extension of the zero-plus-orbit dual, but no continuum convergence is inferred from it.

thm:strict-mixture-gap.justification: The certified local inequality proves that retaining all orientation constraints can strictly enlarge the expected-length dual relative to every single-component comparison.
thm:strict-mixture-gap.gap: It is a finite local constant gap and does not establish a separate \(n^{1/4}\) rate gap.
thm:strict-mixture-gap.consumer: It rules out characterization of the orbit benchmark by a maximum of pairwise observed-Gaussian moduli.

thm:union-zero-lower.justification: The vanishing-strength orbit limit proves the constant \(B_{\max}(1-2\alpha)\) obstruction at rank zero under full-union honesty.
thm:union-zero-lower.gap: It lower-bounds rather than exactly evaluates the rank-zero frontier.
thm:union-zero-lower.consumer: Together with the profile interval's \(2B_{\max}\) bound, it yields the rank-zero oracle comparison and strict positivity of the denominator.

lem:block-completion-identification.justification: This isolates the target-specific low-rank recovery map that makes the later expected-length problem causal rather than an arbitrary Gaussian functional.
lem:block-completion-identification.gap: AtheyBayatiDoudchenkoImbensKhosravi2021 develops matrix completion for causal panels at the estimator level; this lemma gives the exact fixed-four-block identity \(D=GA^+F\) under the stated equal-rank anchor condition and feeds a finite-sample union-honest interval problem.
lem:block-completion-identification.consumer: Every positive-rank frontier and every legal-grid target is evaluable from the observed population mean through this recovery map.

lem:finite-action-purification.justification: The cited Dvoretzky--Wald--Wolfowitz theorem removes auxiliary randomization at each finite grid while preserving all finitely many coverage and risk coordinates.
lem:finite-action-purification.gap: DvoretzkyWaldWolfowitz1950 proves finite-coordinate purification; it does not supply the present Gaussian likelihood dual, connected-interval action reduction, normalized stratum risks, or any uncountable-constraint purification.
lem:finite-action-purification.consumer: Each attaining finite-grid kernel becomes a deterministic connected interval before endpoint inflation transfers it to the continuum union.
